title: What Exams Fail to Measure
sentences: I spent most of my school years being told that examinations were fair.
They are, in a narrow sense: everyone answers the same questions in the same room.
What they measure, however, is performance under a very specific kind of pressure.
Some of the sharpest people I know have always tested badly.
They think slowly and thoroughly, which an exam actively punishes.
Others, myself included, learned to produce answers that looked complete.
Looking complete and being right are not quite the same thing.
I only discovered the gap between them once I started working.
Nobody at work has ever asked me to recall something in forty minutes.
They ask instead whether I can find out what I do not yet know.
